query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a thin, oxidation‐resistant aluminide surface coating to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will enable the formation of a protective alumina layer during high‐temperature exposure, thereby improving its oxygen resistance while preserving its intrinsic mechanical properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy that shows 8–16% room-temperature ductility and high-temperature yield strength of 163–530 MPa but suffers from rapid oxidation (pesting) in air.
generation.intervention: Apply a thin, uniform aluminide-based surface coating (e.g., via pack cementation or chemical vapor deposition) designed to react with oxygen and form an adherent Al2O3 scale.
generation.conditions: Exposure in air at approximately 800 °C for up to 5 hours, under low strain rates similar to those previously evaluated (10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹), with preservation of room- and high-temperature mechanical performance.
generation.structural_mediator: A continuous, dense Al2O3 (alumina) scale that forms on the coating, serving as a diffusion barrier to oxygen ingress into the underlying alloy.
generation.mechanism: The aluminide coating reacts with the ambient oxygen upon high-temperature exposure to form a stable alumina scale. This scale minimizes oxygen diffusion into the bulk alloy, preventing pesting and oxidation-related degradation while leaving the alloy’s microstructure and mechanical properties largely unaffected.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated samples, the coated alloy will exhibit significantly reduced oxide scale growth and pesting under 800 °C, 5-hour air exposure, while retaining comparable room-temperature ductility and high-temperature yield strength.
generation.baseline: Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits rapid oxidation (pesting) under these conditions, which degrades its structural integrity and mechanical properties over time.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies to as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloys tested under static or low-strain rate conditions at about 800 °C in air over a period of 5 hours. It does not address cyclic thermal loading or extreme mechanical loads beyond those specified.
generation.uncertainty: It remains uncertain how the coating might behave under extended cyclic thermal conditions or if thermal stresses from the coating–substrate mismatch may induce delamination or affect mechanical performance. The long-term adhesion and integrity of the coating under varied operating conditions also remain to be fully verified.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr samples: one set is treated with the aluminide surface coating using pack cementation (or an equivalent method), while the other set remains untreated. Expose both sets to static air at 800 °C for 5 hours under low strain rate conditions. Post-exposure, evaluate the surface oxidation using microstructural analysis and assess the mechanical properties via tensile tests at room temperature and high temperatures.
measurements: Oxide scale thickness and uniformity (using SEM and EDS)
Adhesion strength of the oxide scale (coating adherence tests)
Tensile mechanical properties at room temperature and at 1000 °C
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated samples do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in oxidation (e.g., a reduction of at least ~50% in oxide scale thickness or evidence of pesting) or if the key mechanical properties (ductility at room temperature, yield strength at high temperature) are not maintained relative to untreated samples, then the hypothesis is falsified.
